finding.claim: purge() calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards its bool result, so purgeAll() runs for any user in context regardless of permissions. Global destructive action reachable without admin. Retained at HIGH; downgrade to MEDIUM if the route is internal-only (route registration not in repo, so reachability unverified).
finding.source: Any authenticated request reaching the purge handler with a *User in context (precondition: valid low-privilege session; route method/path not in repo)
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 — global purge of data

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the user from request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns a bool that is discarded; no enforcement
contrast: rotateKeys uses mustPerm and returns on failure, so the defect is specific to purge

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) is a pure map lookup with no enforcement; mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) is the enforcing variant and is not used by purge; no auth/admin middleware present in repo for this route (registration absent, so upstream control unverified); triage Check 2 plausibility holds (auth-only precondition is realistic); Check 10 self-affecting exception does not apply because purgeAll is global

verdict.guard_found: handlers.go:12-14 checkPerm is a pure map lookup returning a bool, and its result is discarded as a bare statement at handlers.go:26. The enforcing variant mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) is used by rotateKeys (handlers.go:33) but not by purge. A repo-wide grep finds no admin/auth middleware or route registration covering purge.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: handlers.go:26 discards the checkPerm bool, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any user returned by userFrom at handlers.go:25. No effective control exists in the repo, and the attacker only needs a valid low-privilege session if the route is registered without upstream admin middleware, which cannot be verified from the repo, so severity should stay conditional on that.
